paper_title: Cognitive Architectures for Autonomous Agents: A Unified Framework for Memory and Tool-Use

paper_type_recommendation.reason: The current literature lacks a unified theoretical framework for integrating long-term memory with tool-use in LLM agents. This paper synthesizes existing paradigms into a coherent architecture.

number_verification.claim: Park et al. generative agents TrueSkill 29.89

themes.description: Integration of logical reasoning traces with external environment interaction.
Architectures for maintaining long-term state and social coherence.
Learning to interface with external APIs through self-supervised feedback.

research_gap.statement: Current agent architectures are fragmented; they either focus on short-term reasoning traces or long-term social memory, but lack a unified mechanism to chain tools dynamically across long-term memory states.

supported_by.limitation: Inability to use tools in a chain.
Structural constraints of interleaving reasoning and acting.

novelty_statement.statement: We propose 'Nexus', a unified cognitive architecture that treats memory as a dynamic graph and tools as composable functions, enabling recursive tool-chaining grounded in long-term retrieved context.

differs_from.difference: Nexus introduces persistent memory graphs rather than relying on transient prompt context.
Nexus supports multi-step tool chaining, whereas Toolformer is limited to single-step calls.

sharpening_suggestions: Emphasize the recursive nature of the tool-chaining algorithm.
Clearly define the memory object as a formal tuple.

framework_spec.name: Nexus
framework_spec.retrieval_score: S(q, m) = α * cos(q, m_emb) + β * exp(t_now - t_m) + γ * m_imp, where q is query, m is memory, t is time, and α, β, γ are weights.
framework_spec.tool_chaining: 1. Decompose goal into sub-tasks; 2. Retrieve relevant memory; 3. Select tool; 4. Execute; 5. Update memory with result; 6. Evaluate progress.
framework_spec.training_objective: Maximizing task success via iterative refinement of reasoning traces.
framework_spec.complexity_and_cost: O(N*M) where N is memory size and M is tool-call depth; moderate compute overhead due to recursive retrieval.

hypotheses.statement: Recursive tool-chaining improves performance on complex multi-step tasks compared to single-step tool use.
hypotheses.confirmed_if: Nexus outperforms baseline by >5% on multi-hop benchmarks.
hypotheses.refuted_if: Nexus performance is equal or lower than baseline.

hypotheses.statement: Dynamic memory retrieval reduces hallucination in grounded reasoning tasks.
hypotheses.confirmed_if: Nexus shows lower hallucination frequency in open-world environments.
hypotheses.refuted_if: No significant difference in hallucination rates.

hypotheses.statement: Memory importance weighting improves long-term coherence in social simulations.
hypotheses.confirmed_if: Nexus achieves higher TrueSkill ratings in interview evaluations.
hypotheses.refuted_if: Nexus fails to improve over baseline coherence.

unfair_comparisons_to_avoid: Comparing small model results to large model benchmarks from literature.

outline.title: Introduction
key_points: The gap between reasoning and memory.
Three contributions: Nexus architecture, recursive chaining, memory-grounded retrieval.
